discovery: Evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background using pulsar timing arrays

nominees.name: Michael Kramer
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute for Radio Astronomy, Bonn, Germany

motivation: In June 2023, pulsar timing arrays in North America, Europe/India, Australia and China jointly reported evidence for a gravitational-wave background at nanohertz frequencies. The key signature was the Hellings-Downs angular correlation in the arrival times of millisecond pulsars spread across the Galaxy. This opened a new band of the gravitational-wave spectrum, about ten orders of magnitude below LIGO, and points to a cosmic population of supermassive black-hole binaries. It took two decades of nanosecond-precision timing, new instruments and signal processing, and careful noise modelling to turn the Milky Way into a detector. Maura McLaughlin co-founded and led NANOGrav. Michael Kramer drove the European array, MeerKAT timing and the relativistic-pulsar precision that made it possible. George Hobbs led the Parkes Pulsar Timing Array and built the International PTA. Together their work founded nanohertz gravitational-wave astronomy, a discovery as significant as the first LIGO detection.
